title: MemMap: An Adaptive and Latent Memory Structure for Dynamic Graph Learning

problem.claim: Dynamic graph learning must update node representations when new temporal events are observed.

gap.claim: Most previous graph learning methods generate node representations from directly connected neighbors, creating a need for an alternative latent semantic space.

contributions.claim: Introduces MemMap, an adaptive and evolutionary latent memory space for dynamic graph learning in which each memory cell corresponds to an evolving graph topic.
Generates node representations from semantically correlated memory cells rather than from linked neighbors.
Reports that the latent memory structure can capture dynamic graph changes and balance global and local message passing through semantic similarity.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present MemMap as a novel memory structure for updating node representations in dynamic graphs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report experiments on real-world datasets with comparisons against state-of-the-art methods.
The authors report that MemMap captures dynamic graph changes and forms a compact evolving structure organized by latent graph-node topics.
The authors report that generating representations from latent semantic space is more effective and efficient than generating them from directly connected neighbors.

narrative_sequence.summary: Dynamic and evolutionary real-world graphs motivate dynamic graph learning.
A central challenge is updating node representations when new temporal events occur.
MemMap introduces an adaptive latent memory structure whose cells represent evolving graph topics and whose correlated cells generate node representations.
Experiments on real-world datasets compared MemMap with state-of-the-art methods, and the authors report advantages for capturing changes and balancing global and local message passing.

source_observation.claim: The reported memory space may contain fewer cells than the graph has nodes.

interpretation.claim: A compact latent structure could reduce the representational burden while connecting semantically similar nodes.

application.claim: For dynamic graph systems, consider maintaining adaptive latent semantic structures alongside or instead of direct-neighbor aggregation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when latent memory is preferable across graph types, event patterns, or task settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, tasks, baselines, metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not describe the MemMap update mechanism or training procedure.
The abstract does not quantify the number of memory cells or efficiency gains.
